summary.headline: Aztec H2 FY26 revenue up 12.4% YoY to ₹47.61 cr; FY26 revenue up 9.2% to ₹96.53 cr with EBITDA margin at 14.3%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹96.53 cr (+9.2% YoY) and H2 revenue of ₹47.61 cr (+12.4% YoY). EBITDA rose 9.6% to ₹13.96 cr, with margin at 14.3% versus 14% a year earlier, while PAT was ₹7.41 cr, held back by higher depreciation, write-offs (up 85%), lower other income and tax. Management said the growth was below the earlier double-digit guidance and that it will prioritise margins over top-line growth. Capex is planned across infrastructure, exports and technology, but the absolute amount has not been disclosed and funding (internal accruals, debt, possibly equity) is still under evaluation.

financial_highlights.change: Impacted by higher depreciation, write-offs (+85% YoY) and lower other income
Tech infrastructure, systems, manufacturing, digital platforms

segments.name: Jettings (acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹19.22 cr (+7%); EBITDA up over 18%. Employee cost down 20% and operating expenses down 11%, while purchases rose 41.5% to about ₹9 cr. Interest cost is the remaining weak point due to working capital intensity.

segments.name: Consumables (inks, wash, makeup/cleaner fluids)
segments.commentary: Management said makeup and cleaner fluids grew about 15% YoY and inks about 12.5% YoY in selling volumes. Ink and solvent mix is expected to shift as ink formulation is modified to reduce solvent consumption.

segments.name: Printers (CIJ, TIJ, DOD, laser, TTO, PIJ)
segments.commentary: An installed base of 8,000+ printers was cited, with 1,550 printers sold in FY26 per the call; the group-level tally was not reconciled on the call. Extrusion accounts for the largest share of CIJ applications (about 85%), and CIJ is said to make up ~95% across extrusion, food and FMCG.

segments.name: Government tenders and automation projects
segments.commentary: Two government tenders were won last year and more are in the pipeline. Management says project business is multi-month, high-ticket and built around a separate North and South team.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated sustainable double-digit medium-term growth but did not give a near-term number, and said margins take priority over top-line growth.
Management said it expects to hold the current EBITDA margin (about 13-14%) in FY27 and does not plan to chase top-line growth at the expense of margins.

Capex is split broadly as 41% infrastructure capacity, 30% exports and global expansion, 8% tech and ERP, 3% R&D and 5% product development and other initiatives. The absolute amount is still under board consideration.
Management said the full-year effect of recent investments will show up in FY27, and free cash flow is expected to rise with that.
capex_capacity: Capex is planned over the coming period across infrastructure capacity (41%), exports and global expansion (30%), tech and ERP (8%), R&D (3%) and other product development (5%). The absolute rupee amount has not been disclosed.
Funding is planned through internal accruals and debt, which management said have high visibility; equity remains under evaluation.
Backward integration: inks, wash and solvents are about 100% in-house; about 95% of the ink portion is integrated. Printer spares are 40-50% indigenised, with more in beta testing.
The Jettings integration progressed through the year-end and is contributing to operational synergies.
Management said the capex was deferred because of Middle East conflict visibility, and it was not committing advances until the outlook clears.
demand_pricing: Management said extrusion (PVC/CPVC pipes and wires) slowed in FY26 due to Middle East conflict effects on input costs, while FMCG and food did not see substantial slowdown.
Customer mix: extrusion is the largest vertical; others include food/pharma/FMCG, industrial equipment and automation, agriculture, packaging and printing, and 'others' at about 16.6% of top line.

Pricing: management said the company passes input cost increases on through service-linked AMCs, and that customers negotiate but ultimately accept. Inventory was built only to the extent customers could absorb, and the company declined to stock up at war-peak prices.
After-sales economics: management cited ₹80,000-1,20,000 per printer per year for extrusion customers (about ₹60,000 for some pharma and FMCG accounts), roughly equal to the printer cost per year.
Competition: management cited a fully integrated ink-to-printer model, backward integration and import-duty advantage over MNCs with overseas manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Installed base of 8,000+ printers versus 1,550 sold in FY26 does not reconcile with the prior 5,000+ base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the installed base includes Jettings-led sales and after-sales, and that the group-level number is correct. It was not broken down by company.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook: why should double-digit growth return after the 9.2% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Devraj Pandya said growth is the result of recent investments flowing into revenue over time, and that margins will be protected even if top-line guidance is missed. He cited diversification beyond extrusion as a hedge.

qa_highlights.question: Jettings acquisition: benefits achieved and performance versus plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jettings' revenue rose 7% to ₹19.22 cr and EBITDA margin rose to 10.2%, with lower employee and operating costs. It said the interest cost is still high because of working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: Government tenders and automation: size and timing of contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two tenders were won last year with more in the pipeline and that project business is multi-month, with a separate North and South team. The revenue size was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Capex amount and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the absolute capex is under board consideration and that broad percentage allocations are set. Funding is planned through internal accruals and debt; equity is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Iran/Middle East conflict on raw material prices and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built only to customers' absorption capacity, and that service-linked AMCs make it easier to pass through costs. It expects the disruption to ease but said post-ceasefire effects can last 3-5 months.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 9.2% fell short of the earlier double-digit framework, and PAT growth was held back by depreciation, write-offs and tax.
Supply chain: heavy reliance on imported printheads and electronic components; management acknowledged this and cited a Taiwan Strait scenario as a risk.
Equity dilution: management said equity is still under consideration, while an analyst argued against it given the market capitalisation of about ₹123 cr versus reserves of about ₹44 cr.
Jettings working capital intensity and high interest cost.
Middle East conflict effects on raw material cost, CPVC/PVC demand and extrusion customer spending.
Customer concentration in extrusion; management is building vertical heads for FMCG/pharma, agriculture and extrusion.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on margins and cash generation, but cautious on top-line growth and capex. It repeatedly deferred to later disclosure on capex size, indigenisation progress and the printer count reconciliation, and it answered several questions only partly.
key_quotes: The strategy of Astec is very simple: we would be providing the world-class solutions at the price which is a win-win for both Astec and the customer, and whatever we commit, we deliver.
We won't be focusing on exorbitant increase in top line, we would be focusing more on our margin profiles.
So we are very cautious in managing our cash, we are very cautious in deploying our resources as far as the CAPEX is concerned.

adds.what: Capex split across infrastructure capacity (41%), exports/global expansion (30%), tech/ERP (8%), R&D (3%), product development (5%); absolute amount not disclos

growth.why: No numeric near-term revenue guidance: management reiterated only 'sustainable double-digit' medium-term growth, said it will prioritise margins (~13-14%) in FY27, and walked back the earlier double-digit target; capex is sized only in percentages with no amount, timeline or board approval, so backing is vague.
